text: You didn't need it.
You didn't even want it.
Until you saw the other option.
Behavioural economist Dan Ariely tested a real magazine offer on his students.
Online only: fifty-nine dollars.
Print only: one hundred and twenty-five.
Print and online: also one hundred and twenty-five.
Nobody chose print only.
Eighty-four percent chose print and online.
Then he removed the print-only option.
Suddenly, most people chose the cheap online version instead.
That useless middle option was a decoy.
It wasn't there to be bought.
It was there to make the expensive one look like a bargain.
And it's everywhere.
Small, medium, and large popcorn.
Three phone plans.
"Was ninety-nine, now forty-nine."
So next time, cover up the other options, and ask: would I still want this on its own?
